summary: Master password / bcrypt sign-in feature fully verified end-to-end. Backend: 8/8 pytest passed (login success, wrong pw 401, unknown email 401 same message, member-without-hash 401, brute-force lockout on 6th attempt with fresh random email, change-password + revert cycle, wrong current 400, short new pw 400). Restart-survival verified: after `supervisorctl restart backend`, login with OL1-84A7-EDE3-E64C returns 200 (seed_master_password respects envSha marker and does not clobber). MongoDB: owner.password_hash starts with $2b$12$, member has no hash (and is revoked as noted in test_credentials.md), login_attempts has identifier_1 index, user_sessions has session_token_1 index. Frontend: logged-out landing shows Login page with password form + Google button; bad password renders inline 'Invalid email or password.' (string, no crash); real login lands in Command Center with no Google redirect; Team & Approvals shows Master Password card with all mp-* inputs; save button correctly disabled when current empty or new<8 chars; mismatched confirm shows toast "New passwords don't match.". Master password left as OL1-84A7-EDE3-E64C (verified via final /api/auth/login = 200).
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py login_attempts cleanup on successful login only removes docs for that ip+email — orphan attempt docs for random fake emails from brute-force tests accumulate. Consider a TTL index on updatedAt (~30 min) so login_attempts self-cleans.

auth.py: seed_master_password() only seeds the FIRST-created owner (sort created_at asc). If a second owner is ever created, they won't get the env password — acceptable given single-owner design but worth a comment.

MasterPasswordCard: save disabled logic uses next.length<8 but no client check on confirm length; UX-wise fine (server enforces), but you could disable on confirm.length<8 too to short-circuit the mismatch toast.

Login.js formatApiErrorDetail is defensively safe against FastAPI 422 arrays — good; consider extracting to /lib/errors so change-password toast can reuse it (currently MasterPasswordCard renders detail directly which would crash if server ever returned a Pydantic array error).
seed_data_creation: None. Brute-force test only creates login_attempts docs under a random fake email (self-cleans logically after lockout expiry).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Feature is stable. Restart-survival works via envSha marker in db.state 'master_seed'. Brute-force lockout is per ip+email — any lockout tests MUST use a random fake email (never owner.test) since test runner shares an IP. Password confirmed = OL1-84A7-EDE3-E64C. member.test@example.com is status=revoked from a prior E2E run (as noted in /app/memory/test_credentials.md) — restore per that file if member-flow tests are needed.
